conditions.rule: Check for causes of changes in skin colour
conditions.quote: Is the skin yellow, too dark, too light or absent of colour?
conditions.note: No red-box header for the skin-colour complaint; trigger is the opening question. Discoloration of skin (finding) as the complaint; it is not a recorded common symptom.

conditions.rule: Check for causes of changes in skin colour

conditions.quote: Where are patches on body? Lower legs

elements_not_encoded.reason: Haemoglobin has no observable or unit in the language; the priority rule fires less often than the page intends (jaundice with low Hb alone is not flagged).

judgment_calls.decision: Due_to and priority use (or clinical_finding Jaundice, active_condition Jaundice) so both a recorded jaundice and the probable diagnosis from yellow skin fire the red box.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Only clinical_finding Jaundice (brief default when nothing diagnoses it probable); here the page itself says jaundice likely.

judgment_calls.decision: All of: generalised congenital achromia of skin, white hair, iris hypopigmentation ("Present from birth. Involves skin, hair and eyes").
judgment_calls.alternatives: Generalised + congenital achromia alone; the and may make the rule rarely fire.

judgment_calls.decision: Scaly skin AND (dark patch on trunk OR light patch anywhere).
judgment_calls.alternatives: Require trunk site for light patches too; page says "usually" so site not required.

judgment_calls.decision: Not encoded; red box encoded as Shock or SBP < 80 per the shared decision.
Discoloration of skin (finding). Hyperpigmentation/Hypopigmentation/Achromia of skin are not its descendants, so recording only those does not fire the task.
judgment_calls.alternatives: or of several triggers, but those forms are checked for, making the check self-referential.
